preview: Interview experience of Narayani Bokde at Hilti for an internship, covering the online assessment, technical round, and HR round.
content: HTSI Interview Experience Narayani Bokde Third Year Computer Engineering Location: Pune Stipend: 80,000 INR. Timeline Registrations 30th to 31st August PPT 6th Sept, 6:00 pm OA 7th Sept, 11:00 am Interview 8th Sept, 10:00am - 3:00pm Online Test Type Timer No. of questions Coding None 1 Aptitude 30 minutes 30 CS Fundamentals None 30 The test had 61 questions for 90 mins in total and was held on mettl, we had to allow camera and microphone access. Coding Section Given a list of numbers indicating the window number and a number indicating the window number to be accessed, modify and return the list after applying the MRU strategy. In order to implement the Windows screen switch shortcut (WIN + TAB), we need to use a Most Recently Used (MRU) strategy which brings the recently accessed window to the front. Example: input list - [5, 2, 3, 4, 1], window number to be accessed - 2 output list - [2, 5, 3, 4, 1] Here, as Google Chrome is being accessed at the moment, the next time we use WIN + TAB, it will appear at the front of the list. I had already seen this question in the previous year's Interview Experiences so I did not need to spend too long to even read the question as I already knew what needed to be done. There were 10 test cases – 7 sample test cases, 2 necessary cases and 1 Edge case as listed on Mettl. I couldn’t solve 1 Necessary case and 1 Edge case. There were ample choices for the preferred programming language for the question, I chose c++. Other students got different coding questions but they were also repeated from last year’s, so go through those Interview Experiences as well. Aptitude Section This section had a 30 minute timer on it and had very basic questions, even easier than NTSE MAT. There were 30 questions in total and the last 10 required math. Computer Fundamentals This section had questions based on - Topic No. of questions Description DSA 6 Although very basic, you could easily make a mistake. OS 6 Pretty objective and theoretical, some were factual while others very basic. OOPs 7 These used JAVA terminology so I had a tough time co-relating it with c++, although very easy. CN 6 I had not covered CN, so I randomly marked these. DBMS 5 Again, very easy and basic questions. With this section, I ended my OA for Hilti. I had 15 minutes left in the end where I decided to go through a few questions again just in case if they were wrong, and yes I had made silly mistakes in DSA so I quickly got them right and submitted. Around 21 students were shortlisted for the interview rounds. The list was released on the same day at 5:30pm. I had ample time to revise SQL and spent the rest of the day sleeping. Technical Round The TPO CRs had informed us that students will be called randomly for the interview, so I didn’t have an idea as to when I would be called in. So while I waited, I was also going through the questions that other interviewees were getting asked. Those mainly consisted of project related questions and common OOPs questions, as well as Linked List implementation/Strings questions or classic DSA questions like Largest Histogram. Almost all of them had only one interviewer and lasted for 40 minutes, so I sat relieved. At 12 noon, I was asked to join the Microsoft Meet where to my surprise I was greeted by two interviewers. They introduced themselves, after which I introduced myself as well. Keep a 1.5 to 2 minutes introduction of yourself ready, which you can use in every interview that you sit for. I had sat for 2 companies prior to this one so I would change mine a little wherever I found the need to. The basic flow should be : >> Name, Branch, CPI >> Current interests (for me it was Web Dev, taking part in hackathons/working in various teams, and DSA) >> Achievements (name the competitions and track prizes if any) >> Current and past Club Activities >> Hobbies. In the meantime, they went through my resume and also checked up on my LinkedIn Profile, so definitely ensure that your profile is up to date there. I was expecting Project based questions in depth but they just asked me to describe a little about all of them that I had in my resume. After this, they asked me a little about MongoDB and the difference between NoSQL and SQL. They asked me whether we can have structured data in NoSQL databases, the answer to which is yes. After that they asked me OOPs questions, since they were very fundamental, I tried to be as clear and innovative in the examples as I could. The questions were: 1. Give an example to explain the 4 pillars of OOPs (I took the example of pianos in general since I had mentioned that in my hobbies) 2. What is the difference between Abstraction and Encapsulation? 3. Why is Abstraction important? We moved on to DSA, where one of the interviewers directly pasted a question in the chat : Reverse alternate levels in a perfect binary tree. I had already solved this question on Leetcode in June, and luckily I could recall how to solve it. I gave a level order traversal approach to it. I typed the entire function down on notepad in c++ with all the correct syntax and comments and gave a dry run as well, but the interviewer was not satisfied and changed the question to it not being a perfect binary tree anymore. Frankly speaking, I did not know how to solve the new variation, I just had one thing in my mind that I needed to keep a track on the parent, so swapping the children in a DFS/inorder fashion seemed the answer to me. I said exactly that, to which they still weren't satisfied, so they moved on to the next question. They gave me a puzzle to solve, 10 balls in 5 lines. This is a pretty classic puzzle that I had never heard of before, so I opened Paint and started brainstorming. Since I had little to no idea on the rules to this puzzle, I asked all the doubts that came to my mind. After 3-4 minutes of thinking out loud, I suddenly realized that drawing a star would do the trick. The interviewer told me that the time is up and we concluded the meet. He did say in the end that they were looking forward to see more of me, but I did not keep my hopes high as I did in my previous interviews only to not get invited for HR. The interview lasted for exactly 40 minutes, after which the panel updated that they will be resuming after lunch break at 2:00pm. Lucky enough, I got called in right at 2:00pm for the HR round. HR Round I was flabbergasted when I was asked to join for this round, and I quickly got in front of my laptop and with a huge smile sat for the interview. I was greeted by a female interviewer this time and she gave a very detailed introduction followed by which I gave mine. I made sure to emphasize on my soft skills while keeping the technical aspects a little less in the limelight. She went through my resume in great depth and was very surprised with the amount of hackathons that I had participated in and/or won track prizes in. She then asked me very HR type questions, but mainly on how I am able to juggle between college and hackathons and club activity. All the questions were based on hackathons, so it really helped me a lot considering that was the strong point for me. Wherever she asked me questions not based on something technical, I made sure to set the environment that way because I had appeared for an HR only interview previously for another company, and I had messed that up very badly by not answering in technical ways at all. Regardless, she was very impressed with my resume and the amount of time I had spent my entire second year doing various things and still being able to maintain a good pointer. In the end, I asked her a few questions that I was really curious about based on the introduction she gave me and not just the typical questions you’re supposed to ask in the end. The interview lasted for 35-40 minutes and I finally slept in peace after that. I did not keep my hopes high because I had gotten rejected previously even after giving a very good interview, so I told myself and my parents not to get too excited. At 6pm, they released a list of 4 students that were offered the internship opportunity, and I was lucky enough to be one of them. Resources 1. For DSA, I used Strivers SDE Sheet, although many others suggest 450DSA as well. Just make sure that you are solving questions properly and revising them at least once after a month or so, otherwise it’s 10 times easier to forget it. 2. For OS and DBMS, I used multiple resources depending on how much time I had to revise. Obviously, I got to cover these subjects thoroughly in my 4th sem, so make the most out of that. a. Striver’s revision sheet b. InterviewBit 3. For SQL, I went through GateSmashers’ 10 videos on SQL for revision as well as my lab assignments for the same. 4. For OOPs, I had to prepare thoroughly so I went through various geeksforgeeks articles on topics as basic as four pillars of OOPs to stuff very specific like VPOINTERS and VTABLES. Make sure you know the differences between c++ and java, and OOPs topics specific to java in case you have only done c++. 5. For HR, I don’t know how to prepare, but maybe go through indiabix for that as well as aptitude questions. Tips 1. Don’t panic, this is not the end of the world. Opportunities are readily available for you if you have prepared with all your might. 2. Resume matters a lot, so make sure you get it reviewed by your seniors. Even last minute changes work wonders. 3. Keep calm during interviews, make sure you think out loud while brainstorming for an answer. 4. Don’t pause for too long, even if the interview is about to end, avoid that. Make yourself look as interactive as possible, ask questions so that the interviewer doesn't lose their interest in you. 5. Be confident, obviously. 6. Don’t burn yourself out, otherwise it’ll get tougher to do DSA etc when it’s high time. Feel free to contact me on LinkedIn or email me at narayanibokde232@gmail.com!
